sections.heading: What makes this poster style feel like your family?

blocks.text: Bob’s Burgers-inspired artwork works because it combines simple cartoon shapes with very specific personality. Thick outlines, expressive eyebrows, cosy colours, and a little everyday awkwardness can make a portrait feel instantly familiar. The goal is not to copy a copyrighted character or place your family inside an episode. Instead, your household becomes a group of original cartoon characters drawn in a recognisable visual language.

Your hair, glasses, clothing, expressions, favourite objects, and family dynamics all help distinguish the final piece. A parent might be holding a spatula, a child might be guarding the fries, or a dog might be waiting beneath the counter. These small choices turn a generic cartoon into a personal poster with its own joke and story.

sections.heading: Choose the right photo for your custom poster

blocks.text: You do not need a professional photograph. Casual family photos from a kitchen, living room, birthday, holiday, or weekend out can translate beautifully into a Bob’s Burgers-inspired custom poster. The most useful image shows faces clearly and gives the artist enough information to understand each person’s hairstyle, proportions, and usual expression.

items: Use bright, even lighting so facial features and outfit colours are easy to see.
Choose a photo where people are not heavily cropped, blocked, or hidden behind objects.
Include a second image when someone’s face, hairstyle, glasses, or clothing is clearer in another photograph.
Do not worry about perfect poses; goofy expressions and relaxed body language add personality.
For a group portrait, tell the artist who is standing or sitting where if the arrangement matters.

blocks.text: A single photo is enough to get started, but multiple reference images can be helpful for larger families or pets. If the original image has a busy background, the artist can use it as inspiration while creating a cleaner poster composition.

sections.heading: Can a family photo become a Bob’s Burgers-inspired poster?

blocks.text: Yes. A family photo can be transformed into a hand-drawn, style-inspired poster for parents, siblings, partners, children, grandparents, and pets. You can submit one group photograph or provide separate reference photos when everyone was not available at the same time. The artist uses those references to create an original composition that keeps the people and relationships recognisable.

The number of people, preferred pose, and background can affect the composition, so mention these details when ordering. You can also request a family gathered behind a counter, standing outside a fictional burger shop, relaxing at the pier, or posing in a simple colour-blocked setting. The scene should reflect your idea without presenting the artwork as an official image from the show.

sections.heading: Ideas for the scene, outfits, and caption

blocks.text: The background gives your bobs burgers inspired custom poster its own setting. A burger-shop counter is a natural choice, but it is not the only option. A family kitchen, seaside boardwalk, game-night table, takeaway window, or simple pastel backdrop can support the same warm, slightly chaotic feeling.

items: Family behind a counter with a custom burger-of-the-day pun on the sign.
A couple sharing fries with a caption about your anniversary or inside joke.
Best friends at the pier, with one person holding the food and the other choosing the music.
A housewarming gift showing friends gathered around a fictional neighbourhood restaurant.
A birthday scene built around the most energetic or mischievous person in the group.
An anniversary design featuring a playful line such as “Burger of the Month: Us.”

blocks.text: You can suggest outfits, props, a shop name, a burger pun, or a short caption. If you want a particular person to hold an object or stand beside a pet, include that in the order notes. Specific direction helps the artist create a poster that feels like your group rather than a stock cartoon family.

sections.heading: What details should you provide for a commission?

blocks.text: The more clearly you describe your idea, the easier it is to plan a balanced custom bobs burgers portrait. Start with the reference photo, then explain who should appear, what each person should wear, and what mood you want. You do not need to know illustration terminology; a short, ordinary description is perfectly useful.

items: The number of people and pets to include.
Names or simple identifiers so the artist can match each reference image.
Important features such as hair, glasses, facial hair, tattoos, uniforms, or favourite clothing.
The preferred pose, relationship, and left-to-right arrangement.
Background ideas, colour preferences, props, shop signs, or custom text.
Whether the poster is for a birthday, anniversary, wedding, housewarming, holiday, or everyday wall art.
Anything that should be left out, such as a distracting object or unwanted caption.

blocks.text: You will receive a preview before the artwork is finalised. Anime Cabinet includes unlimited free revisions, so you can explain what should be adjusted if a hairstyle, expression, outfit, prop, or layout does not feel quite right. This review stage is especially useful for group portraits, where small details make each original character recognisable.
